Button cell batteries can cause the death of a child if swallowed as they can get stuck and burn through the gut. As someone with small grandchildren I aim to have as few button cells in the house as possible. Here in Australia button cells are packaged to be child-resistant, but it is so easy to drop and loose a small battery when replacing one in a hearing aid.

Thanks. I'll keep going then.

There's something upthread I think I can settle first. You're both half right. user_107 has the mechanism, it's the current doing the damage and not the chemistry burning anything. But chemistry is what sets the voltage, and that's where the gap is. The ones that kill children are 3 volt lithium coins, 20mm across, wide enough to lodge in a small throat and sit there while the electrolysis works. What I hand out all day is zinc air at 1.4 volts. A size 10 is 5.8mm. A 675 is 11.6mm.

Lower and smaller. Not safe. A small enough child can still lodge one, it's still a choking object, and zinc air runs on potassium hydroxide, so a split cell is caustic on its own. I'd treat any swallowed cell as a same day ER trip and not wait for symptoms.

What I'd add is where they actually go missing, because it isn't the fresh card. Zinc air wants about five minutes open to air before it's at full voltage, so you peel the tab and put things down for a bit. The one I find on the floor afterwards is almost never the new cell. It's the dead one that just came out, and I've never seen anyone keeping track of that one.
